title: CategoryTheory.Functor.plus_single_source_square_core
statement: Let C,D,E,B be abelian categories with derived categories. Let M:C→D, V′:D→B, V:C→E and H:E→B be additive functors preserving finite limits and colimits, and e:M⋙V′≅V⋙H. Fix n∈ℤ, objects LA∈D, LB∈C, EA∈B, EB∈E and maps m:LA→M(LB), k:EA→H(EB), cA:EA→V′(LA), cB:EB→V(LB). Suppose cA≫V′(m)=k≫H(cB)≫e⁻¹(LB). Write sF for the canonical degree-n single-complex comparison D⁺F(F-domain[n])≅F(F-domain)[n], and d=(derived-composition(M,V′))⁻¹≫D⁺e≫derived-composition(V,H). Then (single(cA)≫sV′⁻¹(LA))≫D⁺V′(single(m)≫sM⁻¹(LB))=(single(k)≫sH⁻¹(EB))≫D⁺H(single(cB)≫sV⁻¹(LB))≫d⁻¹(LB[n]).

source.place: DerivedCategory.ExactFunctor factorization equations; EtalePullbackSingleComp private single-complex calculations

proof.text: On a single cochain complex the composition and natural-isomorphism comparison equations agree in degree n, and all other components factor through zero objects. Apply localization Q and its factorization naturality to prove the corresponding derived equations. Reflect these equations through the fully faithful bounded-below inclusion. Compose the three equations to obtain the hom form of the single-complex compatibility for d. Postcompose the asserted source square with d.hom and then with H(sV.hom) followed by sH.hom; these maps are isomorphisms. Naturality of sV′ and sH cancels the single comparisons. Functoriality of single reduces the result to the assumed source equation postcomposed with e.hom; cancel e.inv followed by e.hom.
